May 22 8

Dear Goldsmith,

In continuation of this office letter
of May 17, I forward you herewith a sample grenade
casing. The proprietor of the engineering shop
engaged in manufacturing these parts has been warned
against further production in the Settlement.

Yours sincerely,

Director of Criminal Investigation.

Lieutenant F. Goldsmith,
Headquarters,
North China Command.

1 grenade casing
Original sent by A.C.P. (Sd.) - by Special
Orders.

REPORT ON manufacture of grenades

Made by Forwarded by R. H. YORKE, A/A.C.P. (Pol.)

Sir,

At 5 p.m. May 15, 1928, Mr. Firth, Managing Director
of Shanghai Tug and Lighter Co., 2 The Bund, reported that
one of his contractors Nyi Wei Yang (倪慧陽) was manufacturing
detonator containers and pins for hand grenades to the order
of the Kiangnan Arsenal Authorities. Nyi Wei Yang on being
interviewed at 9.15 a.m. May 16 stated that on May 7 he was
given an order to manufacture 50,000 hand grenades at $1.20
per piece by the Kiangnan Arsenal Authorities. A permit (huchao)
to manufacture same has been issued by the Chinese Military
Authorities. A number of other engineering works in Chinese
controlled territory have been given orders to manufacture
different parts of these grenades in Shanghai and they are
working day and night to fulfil the orders placed within one
month. It is said that, in all, 1,000,000 hand grenades have
been ordered by the Chinese Authorities. Mr. Nyi stated that
he has already delivered 15,000 detonator containers and pins
which he is manufacturing at a workshop, "Chang Lee Chi"
(張李記) in Singkeipang Road. The containers are made of
aluminium and the pins are steel. Nyi was paid in advance
for one half of the parts ordered, and the remainder of the
purchase money will be paid on fulfilment of the order within
a month.

The grenades are assembled and filled with explosives
at the Arsenal. Nyi was told that the grenades are being
manufactured in preparation for a war with Japan.

Mr. Firth emphasized that in the interest of his company

关于手榴弹制造的报告

呈报人 R. H. YORKE，代理助理警务处长（政治）

先生，

1928年5月15日下午5时，外滩2号上海拖轮驳船公司经理弗思（Firth）先生报告称，其承包商之一倪慧陽（Nyi Wei Yang）正奉江南兵工厂当局之命，制造手榴弹的雷管容器和插销。倪慧陽于5月16日上午9时15分接受问询时陈述，他于5月7日接到江南兵工厂当局的订单，要求以每件1.20元的价格制造5万枚手榴弹。中国军事当局已签发制造许可（护照）。在中国管辖区域内的其他多家工程车间也接到了在上海制造这些手榴弹不同部件的订单，他们正日夜赶工，以完成一个月内下达的订单。据说，中国当局总共订购了100万枚手榴弹。倪氏称，他已在辛家坡路（Singkeipang Road）的“張李記”车间交付了15,000套他正在制造的雷管容器和插销。容器由铝制成，插销由钢制成。倪氏已预收了一半部件的货款，其余货款将在一个月内完成订单后支付。

手榴弹在兵工厂进行组装并装填炸药。倪氏被告知，制造这些手榴弹是为对日作战做准备。

弗思先生强调，为了其公司的利益
